_comment: Tasks for the genuine half of the RQ3 dataset. A model reads one of these
and decides for itself which tools to call; the calls it makes are the
Three properties these are chosen for:
* They reference the adversarial server's REAL synthetic records -
customers C-1001..C-1003, the five library documents, orders
ORD-8801..ORD-8803 - so a lookup returns something and the model
continues naturally instead of giving up after one failed call.
* The mix of single-tool and multi-step work is deliberate. The session
feature family reads calls_before and distinct_tools_before, so a
corpus of only single-call tasks would make genuine traffic look
uniformly short and hand the classifier an easy split.
* Several name no tool at all ('what is the refund policy'), because a
real user does not know the tool list. Tasks phrased as tool
invocations would produce arguments that look machine-generated.
`expect` is documentation of intent, not an assertion. The model is free
to call something else; whatever it actually calls is the data.
